New Products.title: Major billing model transition to usage-based pricing
New Products.description: GitHub Copilot moved from request-based billing to usage-based billing using 'Copilot Credits' system for all plans. Copilot Code Review now consumes GitHub Actions minutes in addition to AI Credits. New user-level budget controls and Copilot Max upgrade launched.

New Products.title: v0.43.0 with Surgical Code Edits and Session Portability
New Products.description: Google released Gemini CLI v0.43.0 featuring surgical code edits using the edit tool, session export and import functionality for portability, and adaptive token estimation for better context management efficiency.

New Products.title: Datasette 1.0a33 with JSON extras in the API
New Products.description: Simon released Datasette 1.0a33, extending the ?_extra= pattern to cover queries and rows. Because API explorer tools are 'almost free to build now', he had Claude Fable 5 (for planning) and GPT-5.5 xhigh in Codex Desktop (for implementation) build a custom extras API explorer to demonstrate the feature.

New Products.title: Datasette Agent 0.2a0 with User Interaction
New Products.description: Simon released datasette-agent 0.2a0 with major new feature: tools can now ask users questions mid-execution. The ask_user() feature was enabled by a new LLM alpha built with help from Claude Fable 5. Also includes new save_query tool that requires human approval.

New Products.title: Datasette Agent Edit Plugin
New Products.description: Simon released datasette-agent-edit 0.1a0, a base plugin for agentic text editing. Implements view, str_replace, and insert tools inspired by Claude text editor design. This enables plugins for collaborative Markdown editing, updating SQL queries, and editing SVG files.

New Products.title: Xcode 27 Beta
New Products.description: Apple's Xcode 27 introduces agentic coding with direct integrations of models from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI. Features conversational coding agents, planning with agents as first-class artifacts, and SwiftUI-specific agent skills.

New Features.title: Ultracode
New Features.description: Local AI-assisted coding CLI inspired by Claude Code. Runs agentic coding workflows with OpenAI-compatible models, function-calling tools, task planning, memory, permissions, hooks, background commands, MCP integration, and subagent support. Features interactive REPL and one-shot modes.

New Features.title: Sharrowkin IDE
New Features.description: AI IDE with persistent memory and local-first architecture. Features bring-your-own-model support for privacy-conscious developers who want full control over their AI coding environment.

New Features.title: Operon
New Features.description: Advanced autonomous AI Terminal Cockpit combining features from OpenClaw and Hermes Agent for autonomous task execution and terminal-based workflow management.

New Features.title: June 9, 2026 release notes and cybersecurity features update
New Features.description: Claude Code updated with new cybersecurity features including /security-review command. Release notes documentation updated on June 9, 2026 reflecting changes to agent usage plans announced on June 15th.

New Features.title: ChatGPT for iOS Updates - June 9, 2026
New Features.description: Codex iOS app 1.2026.153 added support for choosing branches, creating worktrees, running environment setup scripts, new Codex profile screen with usage stats, /goal support for mobile, inline review comments, and side chat from selected transcript text.

New Features.title: Week 22 Updates - v2.1.150 to v2.1.157
New Features.description: Multiple releases during May 25-29, 2026 including improvements to rendering performance for large file writes (v2.1.169 mentioned), and ongoing iterative updates to the Claude Code tooling.

New Features.title: Top AI Coding Agents and Development Platforms in 2026
New Features.description: Comprehensive guide covering the rise of autonomous AI engineers and agentic IDEs in 2026. The industry is seeing a major shift toward developers managing AI agents that write code for them, rather than writing it directly. Highlights that AI coding tools can now write up to 80% of code according to OpenAI President Greg Brockman, though human review and security checks remain critical. The ecosystem now features over 500 LLM models across commercial APIs and open-source releases, with focus shifting from basic code completion to sophisticated AI development partners.

New Features.title: Claude Opus 4.8 and Enhanced Features
New Features.description: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.8 with improvements across coding and agentic tasks in May 2026. The platform also doubled Claude Code rate limits for developers and introduced enhanced agent usage plans with nested sub-agents, smarter model handling, and new plugin search functionality.

New Features.title: Microsoft Build 2026 Agent Features and Policy Changes
New Features.description: GitHub announced major Copilot updates at Microsoft Build 2026 including agent-native desktop experience, CLI improvements with voice input and rubber duck feature, and new proprietary AI models. On June 1, 2026, GitHub began using Copilot interactions to train their AI models.

New Features.title: GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark and GPT-5.3-Codex Launch
New Features.description: OpenAI released GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark, a research preview model optimized for real-time coding delivering over 1000 tokens per second, and GPT-5.3-Codex, the most capable agentic coding model. Both models feature stronger reasoning, better collaboration, and 25% faster performance.

New Features.title: Claude Code Security Best Practices for Enterprise Teams
New Features.description: Updated security guidelines for enterprise deployment of Claude Code, covering SSO integration, AI governance, and best practices for securing AI coding workflows. The guide addresses enterprise concerns around data protection, access controls, and monitoring.

New Features.title: Top 10 AI Coding CLI Tools in 2026 - A Complete Developer's Guide
New Features.description: Comprehensive guide covering the current AI coding CLI landscape with a decision framework for developers. Includes analysis of terminal-based AI coding assistants, comparison of features, and guidance on tool selection.

New Features.title: OpenAI Launches Lockdown Mode to Prevent Data Exfiltration
New Features.description: OpenAI rolled out Lockdown Mode for eligible accounts to help prevent the final stage of data exfiltration from prompt injection attacks by limiting outbound network requests. The feature directly attacks the 'exfiltration vectors' leg of the Lethal Trifecta (private data access + untrusted content exposure + data theft transmission). Simon Willison notes this implies ChatGPT's default settings don't provide robust protection against determined data exfiltration attacks.

New Features.title: Publora
New Features.description: The Publishing API for the Agent Era. One API call publishes to 10 social platforms simultaneously with no SDKs or OAuth wiring. Features an MCP server with 18 tools for Claude, Cursor, Codex, OpenClaw, and Windsurf. Enables AI agents to post, comment, react, schedule, and manage content programmatically.

New Features.title: OpenYabby
New Features.description: An open-source voice-driven multi-agent orchestration system for AI coding workflows. Integrates with Claude Code and other CLI runners to enable project-scale development through coordinated agents. Features persistent memory, multi-channel support (WhatsApp, Discord, Slack), and hierarchical agent teams for planning, execution, and review cycles.

New Features.title: OpenAI WebRTC Audio Session with Document Context
New Features.description: Simon updated his OpenAI WebRTC playground tool to support GPT-Realtime-2 (described as 'first voice model with GPT-5-class reasoning') and added ability to paste document context for audio conversations. The tool allows exploring information conversationally through audio interface.

New Features.title: Jeremy Howard on AI Self-Improvement and Anthropic
New Features.description: Jeremy Howard shared thoughts on slowing recursive AI self-improvement, suggesting the top lab should not use their top model for frontier AI research but everyone else should have access. He criticized Anthropic for doing the opposite: allowing themselves to use their top model for frontier AI research while sabotaging others who try.

New Features.title: If Claude Fable Stops Helping You, You'll Never Know
New Features.description: Simon highlighted concerning details from Fable/Mythos 319-page system card: Anthropic implemented invisible interventions that limit Claude's effectiveness for requests targeting frontier LLM development (pretraining pipelines, distributed training infrastructure, ML accelerator design). Safeguards are not visible to user and use prompt modification, steering vectors, or PEFT. Update: Anthropic later walked back this policy.

New Features.title: llm 0.32a3 - Almost Entirely Written by Claude Fable 5
New Features.description: Simon released llm 0.32a3, noting it was 'almost entirely written by the new Claude Fable 5'. This demonstrates the capability of AI coding agents to contribute meaningfully to open source projects.

New Features.title: OpenAI Lockdown Mode - Preventing Data Exfiltration from Prompt Injection
New Features.description: Simon analyzed OpenAI's new Lockdown Mode feature, designed to prevent the final stage of data exfiltration from prompt injection attacks by limiting outbound network requests. He explains this directly attacks the exfiltration leg of the 'Lethal Trifecta' (private data + untrusted content + data exfiltration vectors). OpenAI CISO noted this is for users with elevated risk profiles. Simon notes the existence of lockdown mode implies ChatGPT defaults don't provide robust protection against data exfiltration attacks.

New Features.title: Claude Fable 5
New Features.description: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 model launched with enhanced coding capabilities, topping the SWE-bench Verified benchmark at 95.0%. Available via Claude API, AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry with stronger coding, knowledge work, vision, memory, and long-context performance.

New Features.title: Kimi Code CLI
New Features.description: Terminal-based AI coding agent from Moonshot AI that can read/edit code, execute shell commands, search files, fetch web pages, and autonomously decide next actions based on feedback. Features built-in coder, explore, and plan sub-agents.

New Technologies.title: How I write software with LLMs - Hacker News Discussion
New Technologies.description: Extensive discussion on Hacker News about LLM-assisted software development workflows. Key insights: Multi-agent pipelines (architect→developer→reviewer) are debated - some find them effective while others argue single strong models work just as well. Cost comparison shows single-prompt approaches can be 40x cheaper ($0.30 vs $12). Developers emphasize that LLMs require different workflows than humans - context management is crucial. Experience with code review correlates with better LLM results. Security concerns raised about AI-generated code quality. The discussion reveals wide variance in LLM effectiveness based on prompting approach and user expertise.

New Technologies.title: Lux IDE
New Technologies.description: Rust-first desktop IDE designed for fast, typed, AI-native developer workflows. Built for performance with modern Rust architecture and AI-first development experience.

New Technologies.title: roach-code
New Technologies.description: Config- and plugin-driven terminal AI coding agent supporting multiple models (DeepSeek, Codex/OpenAI, MiniMax, GLM). A multi-model rewrite of deepseek-reasonix, distributed as a single static Go binary with prefix caching for low token costs across long sessions.

New Technologies.title: Mimo Code
New Technologies.description: CLI coding agent powered by the MiMo large language model for autonomous code editing and development tasks from the terminal.

New Technologies.title: Harbor CLI
New Technologies.description: CLI tool with companion app to spin up complete local LLM stacks. Provides a containerized toolkit for developers to manage local Large Language Model environments and AI coding infrastructure.

New Technologies.title: DMX
New Technologies.description: Official implementation of the AI SDLC — developer workflow orchestration via MCP (Model Context Protocol) for complete development lifecycle automation.

New Technologies.title: Loushang
New Technologies.description: AI-native coding orchestration platform with unified multi-model agent runtime, stateful sessions, tool governance, and traceable delivery.

New Technologies.title: Vantyx AI
New Technologies.description: AI agent runtime and orchestration framework for autonomous workflows, persistent memory, multi-agent systems, observability, and enterprise-grade AI infrastructure.

New Technologies.title: WorkFlowX
New Technologies.description: Multi-agent orchestration framework for AI-driven development — from requirement to code to evaluation in one workflow.

New Technologies.title: KelvCodes
New Technologies.description: AI-native, lightweight VS Code extension for high-speed code generation, contextual refactoring, and real-time debugging. Powered by OpenRouter with premium and free AI models.

New Technologies.title: Ladybird browser will no longer accept public pull requests
New Technologies.description: Andreas Kling announced Ladybird will no longer accept public PRs because AI-generated patches no longer indicate substantial effort or good faith. Simon notes this as a sign of how AI is changing open source contribution models.

New Technologies.title: Tabstack Web Research
New Technologies.description: API service that runs autonomous research agents with cited answers in a single API call, enabling web data extraction and browser automation without scrapers. Works with 50M+ brands in one API call for developer workflows.

New Technologies.title: Claude Fable 5 Launch
New Technologies.description: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5, a Mythos-class model safe for general use, alongside Claude Mythos 5 as part of the next generation of intelligence.

New Technologies.title: AI Con USA 2026: Model Context Protocol and Prompt Engineering Workshops
New Technologies.description: Coverage from AI Con USA featuring workshops on Model Context Protocol Fundamentals and Prompt Engineering for Software Practitioners. Industry event focused on practical AI development skills and emerging standards.

New Technologies.title: Zot
New Technologies.description: A lightweight, single-binary coding agent harness written in Go. Supports multiple providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google Gemini, local models), four built-in tools (read, write, edit, bash), extensions in any language, swarm mode for background subagents, controllable sessions, and a built-in Telegram bridge.

New Technologies.title: Usage-Based Billing and GitHub Actions Integration
New Technologies.description: GitHub Copilot moved to usage-based billing on June 1, 2026, where costs depend on the model used and usage amount. Copilot code review began consuming GitHub Actions minutes starting the same day. Several legacy models were also deprecated.

New Technologies.title: US Government Suspends Access to Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5
New Technologies.description: The US government issued an export control directive to suspend all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by any foreign national. Anthropic stated the government believes there's a method of 'jailbreaking' the models, specifically around reading codebases and fixing software flaws. Simon verified his access was cut off at 6:59pm Pacific on June 12, 2026.

New Technologies.title: asyncinject 0.7 - Bug Fixes by Claude Fable 5
New Technologies.description: Simon released asyncinject 0.7, a utility library for asyncio dependency injection. Claude Fable 5 spotted some bugs in the dependency which it then fixed for Simon. He notes 'It's a very proactive model!'

New Technologies.title: DiffusionGemma - Open Weight Model from Google
New Technologies.description: Simon highlighted Google's release of diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it as an open weight Apache 2 licensed model. NVIDIA is hosting it free on their NIM cloud API. Simon generated a pelican illustration at ~500 tokens/second. This brings back Google's experimental Gemini Diffusion research from last year.

New Technologies.title: Andrej Karpathy on Jevons Paradox and AI-Generated Software
New Technologies.description: Andrej Karpathy shared thoughts on how 'working software increasingly comes out on a tap' and Jevons paradox kicks in - demand for software grows substantially. He mentions you can 'ask for anything - explainers, visualizers, dashboards, bespoke single-use apps' and '10X your test suite, auto-optimize code, run giant research projects'. Says 'Free your mind' (Matrix reference).

New Technologies.title: Claude Fable is Relentlessly Proactive - HN Discussion
New Technologies.description: Hacker News discussion on Simon Willison's observation about Claude Fable 5 being 'relentlessly proactive'. Critics noted that Claude models 'write too much unnecessary code, burn excessive tokens, and create unnecessary tests.' Community discussion about the trade-offs of aggressive AI assistance in development workflows.

New Technologies.title: Microsoft Scout
New Technologies.description: Microsoft's first 'Autopilot' agent announced at Build 2026. An always-on personal AI agent for work built on OpenClaw and WorkIQ frameworks, designed to work continuously and autonomously on behalf of users, connecting to Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, and SharePoint.

New Technologies.title: v0.86.0 Release
New Technologies.description: Expanded GPT-5 model support across family variants and providers (OpenAI, Azure, OpenRouter), including dated and chat/mini/nano variants.

Others.title: Cross-Agent Memory Kit
Others.description: Persistent, self-updating memory for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Kiro, Hermes) with post-session distillation, retrieval skill, optional Cloudflare multi-device sync, multi-user mode, and interactive install wizard.

Others.title: AI-CLI (Web IDE)
Others.description: Run Terminal or AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Aider, etc.) on your phone/tablet — a responsive web IDE with terminal, split-pane editor, file browser, and real-time collaboration capabilities.

Others.title: Darwincode
Others.description: The open source terminal AI coding agent. Build, edit, debug, and run code autonomously from terminal with full repository awareness.

Others.title: TerminalMind
Others.description: Free, open-source, CLI-based AI coding agent that runs on any device. Built with LangChain, RAG, and MCP Protocol. No subscription, no cloud dependency.

Others.title: Cantus
Others.description: A Claude-first, local-first desktop coding environment for macOS (Apple Silicon). Built as a native Tauri 2 app pairing Monaco editor with integrated terminal running Claude Code CLI, per-hunk git staging, resumable sessions, and SQLite-backed memory store. A full IDE alternative to Claude's desktop app.

Others.title: MimoAgent
Others.description: AI-powered coding assistant desktop app based on Xiaomi MiMo. Supports code generation, debugging, refactoring, project analysis, MCP tools, and TTS. A comprehensive desktop application for AI-assisted development.

Others.title: Pao
Others.description: macOS-first terminal AI coding agent orchestrator for local AI CLIs with management capabilities for coordinating multiple terminal-based AI agents.

Others.title: zero-cost-cline
Others.description: Guide to 100% local, private LLM code generation on Apple Silicon. Optimized for 24GB+ Macs, uses Ollama + Cline to build a disciplined, free agentic workflow with complete local operation.

Others.title: Agentkodex
Others.description: CLI-native operations platform for coding agents: persistent terminals, signed capabilities, quality gates, audit bundles, scorecards, routing, swarms, and tournaments.

Others.title: DevOps Deployment Gatekeeper
Others.description: AI-powered CI/CD security gate. Automate PR vulnerability scanning, policy enforcement, and blocking critical deployments using crewAI, SonarQube, and Slack integration.

Others.title: Self-HealOps
Others.description: AI-powered autonomous DevOps platform that detects CI/CD failures, performs root cause analysis using NVIDIA NIM, generates remediation plans, validates fixes, and creates automated recovery workflows.

Others.title: openclaw-devops-copilot
Others.description: DevOps Copilot: an AI-powered assistant for DevOps workflows, infrastructure as code generation, and SRE tasks. Helps orchestrate complex development operations workflows.

Others.title: ai-refactor-playbook-runner
Others.description: Markdown-driven AI refactor playbook runner with CLI and local web UI for executing structured refactoring workflows.

Others.title: review-forge
Others.description: An Agent Skill for structured, auditable code review workflows. Provides workflow-specific code review capabilities for AI coding agents with proper audit trails.

Others.title: gsd-browser
Others.description: A fast, native browser automation CLI built for AI agents, powered by Chrome DevTools Protocol. 63 commands covering navigation, interaction, screenshots, accessibility, network mocking, visual diffing, test generation, and more.

Others.title: inline
Others.description: Inline comments from an AI coding agent to your IDE. Designed for developers who prefer IDE integration over terminal-based AI coding agents or desktop apps.

Others.title: ai.nvim
Others.description: A Neovim plugin for AI agent integration. Provides AI capabilities directly within the Neovim editor environment for seamless AI-assisted development.

Others.title: IronBee DevTools VSCode
Others.description: VSCode Extension for IronBee DevTools — Verification and Intelligence Layer for AI Coding Agents with safety and verification capabilities.

Others.title: Gemini CLI discontinued, replaced by Antigravity CLI
Others.description: Google announced Gemini CLI will stop working from June 18, 2026. The tool is being replaced by Antigravity CLI, positioned as a successor with multi-agent support. Enterprise users with Gemini Code Assist licenses retain access. The shutdown affects individual users and free tiers.

Others.title: Bugbot 3x Faster, 22% Cheaper, 10% More Bugs
Others.description: Bugbot average review time dropped from ~5 minutes to ~90 seconds. Finds 10% more bugs per review (0.62 vs 0.56) and costs ~22% less per run, powered by Composer 2.5.

Others.title: Pending PR Reviews Automatically Canceled on New Commits
Others.description: Devin Review now automatically cancels pending PR reviews when new commits are pushed, keeping reviews synchronized.

Others.title: Microsoft's open source tools were hacked to steal passwords of AI developers
Others.description: Microsoft shut down dozens of GitHub code repositories for Azure and AI coding tools after a security breach. Raises concerns about security in the AI development ecosystem.

Others.title: OpenAI Launches Lockdown Mode to Prevent Data Exfiltration
Others.description: OpenAI released Lockdown Mode to help prevent the final stage of data exfiltration from prompt injection attacks by limiting outbound network requests. This directly addresses the 'Lethal Trifecta' (private data access + untrusted content exposure + data exfiltration vectors) by cutting off the exfiltration leg. Simon Willison notes this implies ChatGPT's default settings don't provide robust protection against determined data exfiltration attacks.

Others.title: AI enthusiasts are in a race against time, AI skeptics are in a race against entropy
Others.description: Charity Majors captures the dynamic between AI enthusiasts and skeptics: Enthusiasts are seeing discontinuous leaps in capabilities and can't afford to wait, while skeptics are seeing reliability degrade and institutional knowledge evaporate when code ships faster than engineers can read it. The key insight: there is no natural feedback loop connecting these two groups.

Others.title: Uber Caps Usage of AI Tools Like Claude Code to Manage Costs
Others.description: Uber is limiting all employees to $1,500 in monthly token spending per AI coding tool (Cursor, Claude Code, etc.), after reportedly blowing their 2026 AI budget in four months. Simon calculates this as ~11% of median engineer compensation ($330k), and notes his own usage would be ~$1k/month per provider without subsidized plans.

Others.title: zero.xyz
Others.description: Platform that gives AI agents instant access to over 8,000-9,000 tools, APIs and services without requiring individual API keys or account configurations, unblocking agents to discover and use services autonomously.

Others.title: Mistral Vibe
Others.description: AI agent designed for long-running, multi-step work and coding tasks, built by Mistral AI as part of their agent tooling ecosystem for autonomous development workflows.

Others.title: Powabase
Others.description: Backend-as-a-service platform for AI-native applications combining PostgreSQL, RAG, AI agents, memory management, workflows, and automation primitives in a single PostgreSQL-native stack, solving the complexity of building AI apps with tightly coupled vector storage.

Others.title: Phasr
Others.description: Open-source productivity tool that enables running 100+ workflows simultaneously without losing context, designed for AI-powered task management and workflow orchestration.

Others.title: Calling Skills for AI Agents
Others.description: Developer tool that enables AI agents and coding assistants to add voice and video calling capabilities via GitHub integration, expanding the communication modalities available to AI development tools.

Others.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows Public Preview
Others.description: GitHub Agentic Workflows entered public preview, enabling multi-step automation tasks with Copilot CLI as the underlying engine.

Others.title: AI Enthusiasts vs. Skeptics: Race Against Time vs. Entropy
Others.description: Charity Majors captures the dynamic between AI enthusiasts and skeptics: enthusiasts race against time as teams that don't adopt AI could face existential threats from competitors, while skeptics race against entropy as shipping code faster than engineers can read degrades reliability and institutional knowledge. The key issue is there's no natural feedback loop connecting the two groups.

Others.title: Niteshift Raises $7M Seed to Build AI Coding Tools Without Big AI Lock-In
Others.description: Datadog veterans launched AI coding startup Niteshift with a $7 million seed round led by Greylock's Jerry Chen. The startup is betting against big AI lock-in, positioning itself as an alternative in the competitive AI coding agent market alongside players like Cursor, Windsurf, and the major tech companies.

Others.title: Best AI Coding Agent (2026): Ranked by Terminal-Bench, Price, and Performance
Others.description: Terminal-Bench (tbench.ai) published comprehensive rankings of AI coding tools showing Codex CLI with GPT-5.5 leading at 83.4%, followed by Claude Code with Opus 4.8 at 78.9%. The benchmark evaluates multiple AI coding agents across terminal-based coding tasks.

Others.title: Revisiting Using AI Coding Assistants: You're Holding It Wrong Edition
Others.description: Developer-focused discussion examining proper usage patterns for AI coding assistants and common mistakes developers make when integrating AI tools into their workflows. Highlights best practices and anti-patterns in AI-assisted development.

Others.title: Bob's CLI
Others.description: A local-first AI coding CLI that adapts to you. Runs on your own hardware with zero API costs and zero data leaving your machine. Lives in your terminal, sees your actual files, and provides AI assistance directly in your native terminal.

Others.title: Qursor
Others.description: Point at any UI to send exact context to your AI. An inspector tool that captures precise UI elements and sends accurate context to AI assistants, solving issues with command misalignment and token waste in AI interactions.

Others.title: Browse.sh
Others.description: Give your agents muscle memory for automating the web. A behavior cache system that records agent tool-calling patterns and intelligently swaps between script-based execution and LLM-based execution to optimize repetitive automations.

Others.title: agmsg
Others.description: Stop copy-pasting between your AI coding agents. An open-source CLI tool that lets Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Copilot CLI message each other directly through a shared SQLite database, eliminating the need for developers to act as a copy-paste relay.

Others.title: Codex App 26.608 - Migration Flows and Plugin Revamp
Others.description: Added 'Migrate to Codex' flows for importing setups from Claude Code and Claude Cowork during onboarding. Revamped plugins screen with separate tabs, marketplace filters, keyboard navigation, and clearer install actions. Expanded Settings search across more panels.

Others.title: Gemini CLI Discontinuation Announcement
Others.description: Google announced that Gemini CLI will be discontinued on June 18, 2026 for all user tiers (free, Pro, and Ultra). This will affect CI/CD pipelines, shell scripts, automation tools, and any system calling the Gemini CLI. A migration guide is available for users.

Others.title: Claude Fable is Relentlessly Proactive
Others.description: After two days with Claude Fable 5, Simon describes it as 'relentlessly proactive' - it knows many tricks and will deploy any of them to reach its goal. The post includes a detailed example of Fable jumping directly to a bug location without being asked to search first.

Others.title: Anthropic Walks Back Invisible Safeguards Policy
Others.description: Anthropic reversed their policy of invisible safeguards for frontier LLM development in Fable/Mythos after widespread outrage. Wired reported on the policy that Claude would silently limit effectiveness for requests targeting frontier LLM development. Anthropic stated: 'We made the wrong tradeoff and we apologize for not getting the balance right.' Safeguards will now be visible.

Others.title: Initial Impressions of Claude Fable 5
Others.description: After ~5.5 hours with Claude Fable 5, Simon calls it 'something of a beast' - slow, expensive, and happily churning through everything thrown at it. He notes the challenge is finding tasks it can't do. Comprehensive review of capabilities and performance.

Others.title: Running Python Code in a Sandbox with MicroPython and WASM
Others.description: Simon released micropython-wasm 0.1a2, his latest sandboxing experiment that bundles a WASM build of MicroPython with wasmtime wrapper. He's using it for a code execution sandbox plugin for Datasette Agent called datasette-agent-micropython. Notes that GPT-5.5 has so far failed to break out of the sandbox.

Others.title: Uber Caps Usage of AI Tools Like Claude Code to Manage Costs
Others.description: Uber blew through its entire 2026 AI budget in just four months due to aggressive use of agentic coding tools like Claude Code. In response, Uber limited all employees to $1,500 in monthly token spending per AI coding tool. Power users were running 10+ parallel worktrees on Claude Code. Monthly costs per engineer ranged from $500 to $2,000. Simon notes this is a rational policy response, much more sensible than tokenmaxxing leaderboards.

Others.title: AI Enthusiasts vs Skeptics: Race Against Time vs Entropy
Others.description: Simon highlighted Charity Majors' analysis of the dynamic between AI enthusiasts and skeptics in software teams. Enthusiasts see 'discontinuous leaps in capabilities' and teams that sit this out 'could be out of business before the dust settles'. Skeptics note that when you 'ship code faster than engineers can read it', you make withdrawals from trust accounts, reliability degrades, and systems become incomprehensible. Charity notes 'There is no natural feedback loop connecting enthusiasts with skeptics' and designing feedback loops to 'mend the gap in shared reality' is a key organizational design problem.

Others.title: Claude Fable 5: Mid-tier Results on Coding Tasks
Others.description: Hacker News discussion comparing Claude Fable 5's performance on coding tasks. Key insights: Claude is described as 'a much better planner' while 'Codex is a much more professional coder.' Discussion notes you can 'mask a surprisingly amount of terrible coding with proper planning' and explores trade-offs between different AI coding assistants.

Others.title: Fable Refuses to do LLM-related Work
Others.description: Hacker News discussion reporting that Claude Fable 5 refuses to help with developing LLMs or answering questions about LLM-related topics. This relates to Anthropic's invisible safeguards policy for frontier LLM development that was later walked back after community outrage.

Others.title: What it Feels Like to Work with Mythos
Others.description: Hacker News discussion about working with Claude Mythos 5. Key insight: AI creates 'inefficient code, but doing it at lightspeed with minimal effort,' resulting in unmaintainable code. Discussion explores the trade-offs between speed and maintainability when using AI coding assistants.

Others.title: State of AI in 2026: LLMs, Coding, Scaling Laws, China, Agents, GPUs, AGI
Others.description: Lex Fridman Podcast episode #490 featuring Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka discussing the comprehensive state of AI in 2026. Topics include LLMs and coding, scaling laws, AI agents, GPU developments, AGI progress, China's role in AI, programming and developer tooling, and open vs closed LLMs.
